result: The R438W mutation severely impairs Trabid's deubiquitylating (DUB) activity, while the A451V mutation retains full DUB activity. In vitro DUB assays showed that R438W exhibited near total loss of activity compared to wild-type, whereas A451V cleaved ubiquitin chains with comparable efficiency to wild-type.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly confirmed these findings, with one stating 'the authors demonstrate that the p.R438W variant impairs the K29- and K63-chain cleavage activity of TRABID' and another noting 'R438W is nearly completely DUB-dead whereas A451V showed normal activity.' The editor affirmed the methods as 'appropriate and validated methodology in line with current state-of-the-art.'

result: The A451V mutation impairs Trabid's binding to the STRIPAK complex while retaining DUB activity. Immunoprecipitation experiments showed that A451V failed to efficiently co-precipitate STRIPAK components including Striatin3 and STRIP1, while maintaining interaction with other substrates like HECTD1.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this finding without challenge. One reviewer stated 'the p.A451V variant reduces binding to the STRIPAK complex' and another noted 'A451V showed normal activity but failed to efficiently precipitate STRIPAK.' The editor confirmed the work 'suggests critical roles for Trabid in the STRIPAK complex.'

result: Knock-in mice harboring R438W or A451V mutations exhibited reduced neuronal and glial cell densities in the brain with incomplete penetrance. Homozygous mutant mice showed reduced Ctip2+ neurons in the striatum and Olig2+ oligodendrocytes in the forebrain and midbrain, with a gene dosage effect observed.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed these findings, with one stating the mice 'exhibit smaller neuronal and glial cell densities' and another noting 'reduced cortical neuronal and glial cell numbers.' The editor praised the 'appropriate and validated methodology' using 'knock-in mice of the patient mutations.' The incomplete penetrance was acknowledged without criticism.

result: Trabid mutant mice exhibited motor deficits consistent with reduced dopaminergic neurons and projections. Both R438W and A451V homozygous mice showed reduced TH+ neurons in the substantia nigra, decreased TH immunoreactivity in the striatum and motor cortex, and impaired rotarod performance.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these findings, with one noting the mice 'exhibit motor deficits, phenotypes that are consistent with the congenital defects observed in the patients' and another stating 'reduced TH+ neurons and their neuronal processes.' The editor confirmed the work demonstrates 'motor deficits consistent with fewer dopaminergic neurons and projections.'

result: Both DUB and STRIPAK-binding activities of Trabid are required for efficient deubiquitylation of APC in cells. Wild-type Trabid strongly suppressed APC ubiquitylation, while R438W and C443S mutants did not, and A451V only partially reduced APC ubiquitylation.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed this finding, with one stating 'the hypomorphic patient variants are deficient in deubiquitylating APC' and another noting 'both DUB and STRIPAK-binding activities of Trabid are required for efficient deubiquitylation of APC in cells.' No concerns were raised about the ubiquitylation assays.

result: Both DUB-impaired and STRIPAK-binding-deficient Trabid variants impeded APC trafficking to membrane protrusions and microtubule plus-ends. In cells with mutant Trabid, APC formed irregular punctae and aggregates rather than localizing to the lamellipodial leading edge.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these findings without challenge. One reviewer noted 'impaired trafficking of APC to microtubule plus ends' and the editor confirmed the work shows 'both DUB-impaired and STRIPAK-binding-deficient Trabid variants impeded the trafficking of adenomatous polyposis coli (APC) to microtubule plus-ends.'

result: Trabid mutations severely compromised neuronal growth cone formation and neurite outgrowth trajectory. In neurons with mutant Trabid, APC-tdTomato showed broad distribution along neurites rather than accumulating in growth cone tips, and neurites turned back or retracted more frequently.
evaluation: Reviewers affirmed these findings, with one stating 'axonal APC trafficking and neurite outgrowth is disturbed in differentiating neural progenitors' and another noting 'alter APC transport along neurites' and 'consequent defects in neuronal growth cone and neurite outgrowth.' The editor confirmed 'the formation of neuronal growth cones and the trajectory of neurite outgrowth from mutant midbrain progenitors were severely compromised.'

result: The authors propose a mechanistic model in which STRIPAK recruits Trabid to deubiquitylate APC, and in cells with mutant Trabid, APC becomes hyperubiquitylated and mislocalized, causing impaired cytoskeleton organization that underlies the neuronal and developmental phenotypes.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this model without objection. One reviewer stated 'the authors propose a model in which TRABID- and STRIPAK-dependent APC deubiquitylation regulates its axonal trafficking' and the editor affirmed 'the work as presented suggests critical roles for Trabid in the STRIPAK complex mediating APC deubiquitylation.' The model is treated as a reasonable interpretation of the data.

result: ZRANB1/Trabid missense mutations R438W and A451V have been identified in patients with congenital disorders including microcephaly, craniofacial abnormalities, seizures, developmental delay, and autism.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these clinical associations as established facts from prior literature. The editor noted 'two different missense mutations observed in patients in the Trabid/ZRANB1 gene associated in children with a range of congenital disorders including reduced brain size.' No concerns were raised about the patient mutation data.

result: The authors propose that the diverse patient phenotypes may be explained by abnormal specification or migration of neural crest cells, and that the irregular cellular architecture in mutant mouse brains may reflect errant migration of neural crest or neural progenitor populations in early embryogenesis.
evaluation: This is explicitly presented as speculation by the authors ('we propose,' 'we can only speculate'). Reviewers did not comment on this hypothesis, neither supporting nor challenging it. The editor noted 'many of the reviewer comments were focused on potential next experiments' suggesting this mechanistic speculation was not a focus of evaluation.
